name: Museum im Ballhaus Imst
kurzbeschreibung: Museum im Ballhaus in Imst: historic 16th-century granary and bale storehouse showcasing Imst town history, sacred art, and the famous Schemenlaufen.
beschreibung:
Overview

The steeped-in-tradition Museum im Ballhaus is located in the historic town centre of the district capital Imst in the Tiroler Oberland at Ballgasse 1, at an altitude of approximately 830 metres. Housed in one of the town's most imposing and architecturally significant secular buildings—a monumental, heritage-listed storehouse dating from the first half of the 16th century—the museum serves as the cultural memory of the Imst valley basin. Across several modern exhibition floors, the museum provides captivating insights into more than 700 years of municipal history, former trade and craftsmanship guilds, and the world-famous Tyrolean Carnival traditions.

History & UNESCO Cultural Heritage

The monumental edifice was constructed around the year 1530 as a civic granary and bale storehouse (a warehouse for bales of cloth and transit trade goods). In 2003, the heritage building was converted into a state-of-the-art municipal museum while meticulously preserving its historic fabric, including massive timber-beam ceilings and thick rubble-stone masonry. An absolute highlight of the exhibition is the section devoted to the Imster Schemenlaufen: this tradition-rich carnival ranks among the oldest and most spectacular custom rituals in the Alps and in 2012 became the very first Austrian custom inscribed on the global UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. On display are masterfully carved wooden masks (Larven) of the Roller and Scheller figures, ornate traditional costumes, and historical documents from the carnival archives. Other focus areas illuminate the 18th-century era of the Imst canary bird merchants, textile finishing, valuable Gothic sacred art treasures, and paintings by regional artists such as Thomas Walch.

Visit & Getting There

The Museum im Ballhaus Imst is open year-round: Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday from 14:00 to 18:00, and Saturday from 09:00 to 13:00 (closed on Sundays and public holidays; special group tours available upon request at any time). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €5.00, seniors and students approx. €4.00, while children and teenagers under 18 enjoy free admission! With the regional Urlaubspass Imst, admission is completely free. Getting there by public transport: take the ÖBB train to Imst-Pitztal station, then take Imst town bus line 1 or 2 directly to the Imst Rathaus or Stadtplatz stop (from there it is just a two-minute walk to Ballgasse). By car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (Imst exit); parking is available in the nearby Stadtplatz underground car park.

Tips

During its renovation, the historic Ballhaus was equipped with exemplary barrier-free access: thanks to a modern glass lift, all floors and exhibition galleries are step-free and accessible for wheelchair users and pushchairs. Combine your museum visit with a walk along the Imster Brunnenweg (fountain trail) or through the wildly romantic Rosengartenschlucht gorge, the entrance to which lies just a few minutes' walk from the museum.
